{
  "research_question": "Does intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) modality, visual modality, or their combination differentially modulate mouse navigation performance as measured by time-to-target, success rate, path efficiency, average speed, and angular dispersion?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the between-subjects factor with 5 levels",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence as the ANOVA-equivalent approach",
    "Given the unbalanced design (n ranges from 3,505 to 48,846 across paradigms), use Type III sum of squares to properly account for unequal sample sizes",
    "Specify significance threshold at alpha=0.05 for omnibus tests"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous variables showing significant ANOVA results, perform pairwise comparisons between all 10 possible paradigm pairs using Tukey's HSD or Games-Howell procedure depending on variance homogeneity",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use pairwise z-tests for proportions with correction",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs ICMS Only (visual contribution), Combined vs both visual conditions (ICMS contribution), both stimulated groups vs Sham (overall stimulation effect)",
    "Report effect sizes (Cohen's d for continuous variables, odds ratios for Success) alongside p-values"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction at q=0.05 across all post-hoc tests within each response variable; apply separate family-wise correction per outcome to maintain interpretability while controlling for the burden of 10 comparisons per variable × 5 variables = 50 total comparisons",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response variable and the five performance metrics as predictors. This is explicitly recommended over ordinary linear regression or multiple ANOVAs because: (1) stimulation paradigm is categorical with no natural ordering, making it an ideal response variable; (2) the model directly estimates the probability of each stimulation condition given observed performance, reversing the typical ANOVA direction and yielding actionable predictions; (3) it naturally handles multicollinearity among the correlated performance variables through regularization if needed; (4) with 76,655 observations, the model will have excellent power for estimating 4×(5 predictors)=20 parameters. Alternatively, a random forest classifier could be used if nonlinear interactions are suspected, but multinomial logistic regression provides interpretable coefficient estimates for scientific inference.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed by experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation in trial sequences within mice",
    "Normality: Assess via Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals and Q-Q plots; given large N (76,655), Central Limit Theorem provides robustness, but severe skew in Path Efficiency (max=29.8 vs mean=0.47) suggests log-transformation may be needed",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test for each continuous variable; unequal variances expected given Sham's poor performance (mean Success=0.27 vs Combined=0.78), necessitating Welch ANOVA or Games-Howell post-hocs as appropriate",
    "Multicollinearity: Compute VIF among predictors for multinomial model; expected correlation between Success and Time-to-Target (successful trials likely faster)",
    "Complete separation check for multinomial logistic regression: Verify no performance variable perfectly predicts any single paradigm"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Significant omnibus effects for all five response variables based on paradigm means: Combined shows fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s) and highest Success (0.78), Sham shows slowest (4.68s) and lowest (0.27)",
    "Pairwise comparisons expected to show Sham significantly worse than all stimulated conditions on all metrics",
    "Combined expected to outperform unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) on Success and Time-to-Target, potentially demonstrating additive or synergistic effects",
    "Bright Visual Only (Success=0.785) may approach or match Combined (Success=0.780), while Dim Visual Only underperforms (Success=0.673), suggesting luminance-dependent visual contribution",
    "AD pattern mirrors overall performance: highest in Combined (0.399), lowest in Sham (0.236), consistent with straighter, more directed trajectories under effective stimulation",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only show similar performance profiles (Success ~0.68-0.69, Time-to-Target ~3.05-3.14s), potentially indicating substitutable but suboptimal sensory guidance",
    "Multinomial model expected to achieve high classification accuracy, particularly distinguishing Sham from stimulated conditions; Combined vs Bright Visual Only likely hardest discrimination"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes (Combined n=48,846 vs Sham n=3,505) creates differential statistical power and may inflate Type I error for comparisons involving Combined; effect size estimates for Combined vs others have narrow confidence intervals while Sham comparisons have wider intervals",
    "Success rates near ceiling for Combined and Bright Visual Only (0.78-0.79) may restrict variance and reduce sensitivity to detect subtle differences among best-performing conditions",
    "AD interpretation as angular dispersion assumes consistent coordinate system across trials; no validation data provided",
    "Cross-sectional aggregation across 8 mice with unequal representation (SC21LM=10,986 trials vs SC11LM=7,233) may obscure individual mouse differences; mouse as random effect not addressed in current design",
    "Temperature=1.0 in model specification may indicate LLM-based data generation or processing; if so, replicate consistency and ground-truth validity are unverified",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme outliers (max=29.8, 63× the mean), suggesting possible data quality issues or complex trajectory shapes not captured by efficiency metric",
    "No information on trial-level randomization, learning effects, or session effects; temporal dynamics within and across sessions unaddressed"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Mouse as random intercept to account for individual differences, then examine whether the fixed effects of performance variables on paradigm classification remain stable across mice. Additionally, conduct a dimensionality reduction (PCA) on the five correlated performance metrics to identify a lower-dimensional 'navigation proficiency' construct, and test whether stimulation paradigms differ on this composite score using discriminant function analysis or ordinal regression if a proficiency ranking emerges."
}
